about: Packages whose job a Node built-in or platform API now does. Each row names the API, the Node versions that have it (nodeRange, checked against nodejs.org API history and MDN browser-compat-data), and a one-line migration. Add a row only when the replacement is certain; say what differs in caveat. Rows with fit check-usage change behaviour for some calls and need a read before migrating.

replacements.caveat: left-pad accepts non-strings and numbers; wrap the first argument in String(). Identical for a one-character fill; with a multi-character fill left-pad repeats the whole fill per missing character (leftPad('x', 5, 'ab') is 'ababababx'), where padStart cuts it to length ('ababx').
is-number also returns true for numeric strings such as '5'. If callers pass strings, use typeof x === 'string' && x.trim() !== '' && Number.isFinite(Number(x)) as well.

replacements.migration: flatten(arr)  ->  arr.flat(Infinity);  flatten(arr, depth) (v1, v2)  ->  arr.flat(depth)
replacements.caveat: flat() exists on arrays only: array-like input such as arguments needs Array.from() first. flat() also drops holes in sparse arrays.

replacements.migration: rimraf(path)  ->  fs.promises.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true });  rimraf.sync(path)  ->  fs.rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true });  CLI: rimraf dist  ->  node -e "require('node:fs').rmSync('dist',{recursive:true,force:true})"
replacements.caveat: rimraf v4+ also expands glob patterns and retries on Windows locks; fs.rm does neither. Check the call sites for globs.

replacements.migration: mkdirp(dir)  ->  fs.promises.mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });  mkdirp.sync(dir)  ->  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })

replacements.caveat: make-dir resolves to the directory path; fs.promises.mkdir resolves to the first directory it created (or undefined). Check whether callers use the result.

replacements.migration: import { v4 as uuidv4 } from 'uuid'; uuidv4()  ->  import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'; randomUUID()
replacements.caveat: Only version 4 UUIDs. uuid's v1, v3, v5, v6, v7 and validate/parse have no Node equivalent, so the package is reported as replaceable only when v4 is the only export the source imports.

replacements.migration: import fetch from 'node-fetch'; await fetch(url)  ->  await fetch(url)
replacements.caveat: fetch is available without a flag from Node 18.0.0 but is stable (no ExperimentalWarning) from 21.0.0, which is the floor used here. The response body is a web ReadableStream, not a Node stream, and node-fetch's agent option and response.buffer() do not exist.

replacements.migration: import AbortController from 'abort-controller'  ->  remove the import; use the global AbortController

replacements.caveat: pify also wraps every method of an object and supports multiArgs and includeSync options; util.promisify wraps one function. Check the call sites for those.
